It happened in a few phases and I would say right now we are just on phase 1 or 2, not the near final "redesign' exodus.

First there was some basic censorship, a popular post with some of the oldest (very tame) historical playboy nudes was deleted for instance (It actually spurred interesting discussions) While reddit could post NSFW content. The admins started cracking down on more and more and power users fully took over. Reddit was getting steady stream of people worried about free speech and censorship and was largely filled with very smart people having lengthy discussions.

Then came a much bigger catalyst, the HD-DVD number fiasco (Digg honored a DMCA takedown notice on the number 09 F9 11 02 9D 74 E3 5B D8 41 56 C5 63 56 88 C0, the whole site was taken over with people posting clever variations on such a simple number. https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/a/ae/HD_DVD_Night_Digg_Frontpage_before_rose_blog_post_screenshot.png tons of users were banned, the entire site was basically offline for 48 hours, it was pretty dramatic, a large influx of users moved to reddit at this point, old redditors complained heavily about a decline in quality from diggers. It ended with a halfhearted apology but never addressed deleting people for simply disagreeing with bans and whatnot, so people kept leaving. This seems a lot like the current situation we are in, but perhaps less explosive.

I would say at this point the free-speech minded people were well informed, and the quantity of original content on reddit expanded greatly, for quite a while Digg became simply a mirror of content posted on reddit yesterday, active users on both sites called this out frequently to convert more people to reddit, it kept working.

Through much of this were many teapot storms that had enough influx of users that were enough to bring reddit crashing to the ground or put in to read only mode just about every few days.

Finally the redesign was the nail in the coffin, that caused more of the content-consumer class to jump ship as well because it finally impacted them directly. We are not at this point yet. I imagine Reddit will soon do some major monetization push that will equate.

At the moment the steps we are on is to make Voat have the best content, the best discussions, and keep poaching the best of reddit's creator-class, the rest will follow.
